A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CiteGuard and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. Corresponding content can be matched despite relocations and additions in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original CiteME and CiteMulti experiments, human assessments, action ablations, retrieval analyses, and inference-cost measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds physics/math evaluation, a CiteAgent rerun, expanded citation-set evaluation, and an alternative retrieval-backend experiment.

M1.justification: Section 5.8 introduces an arXiv backend adaptation that disables citation-count and snippet-search actions because of API limitations. The main Semantic Scholar procedure, retrieval operators, iterative exclusion mechanism, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: CiteMulti expands from biomedical and long computer-science excerpts to include physics and mathematics, adding 20 excerpts to the previous 30. The arXiv-backend experiment also tests a different retrieval environment. Together these substantially broaden the scientific domains and search conditions evaluated.

E2.justification: CiteAgent+GPT-4o is newly included in the human-agreement comparison in v4 Table 5; its agreement entry was absent in v3 Table 2. The main accuracy comparisons retain CiteAgent, the same LLM variants, and AI2 Paper Finder. Rerunning CiteAgent does not itself introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: Table 5 extends evaluation to Oracle-in-Set and Agreement at k=1 and k=5. Section 5.8 adds a DeepSeek-R1 evaluation with the constrained arXiv action set. The existing CiteME task, main model lineup, stated hyperparameter policy, and Table 10 non-iterative top-k procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.8 and Table 12 add a portability and backend-sensitivity analysis comparing arXiv with Semantic Scholar. Existing iterative-run, action-ablation, full-text-versus-retrieval, human-context, and appendix case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 newly reports five-run uncertainty for the rerun CiteAgent baseline, 35.4% ± 2.3%, and a Bayesian comparison against CiteGuard with P(Δ>0)=0.98 and a 95% interval of [0.28%, 16.32%]. Existing CiteGuard run counts and single-run Bayesian variant comparisons remain; changed Table 3 outcomes do not establish increased runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces CiteAgent's cited 35.3% with a 35.4% rerun and changes human accuracy from 69.7% to 69.2%; CiteGuard accuracies remain fixed. Table 3 changes the DeepSeek-R1–Kimi-K2 comparison from ΔAcc +5.4, P=0.87 to +19.2, P=0.99. Table 10 revises Gemini top-10 accuracy from 44.7% to 46.2% and DeepSeek-R1 from 71.5% to 84.6% under the same stated procedure. Table 5 replaces agreement values and adds top-5 results. Physics/math results, expanded CiteMulti totals, and arXiv accuracy of 43.1% concern added conditions, not same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same problem formulation, accuracy and agreement equations, retrieval operators, and exclusion-set recurrence. The expanded top-k reporting introduces no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the claimed 17% baseline improvement with approximately 10 percentage points and revise the human reference from 69.7% to 69.2%. The benchmark contribution expands to 50 samples covering biomedical, physics, mathematics, and long-paragraph scenarios. The central attribution, alternative-citation, and near-human-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and 5.5 remove the qualification that DeepSeek-R1's advantage over Kimi-K2 is inconclusive. Section 5.8 interprets backend differences through retrieval capabilities and coverage while arguing for portability. Appendix B adds an argument against memorization based on search terms matching entities in the supplied excerpts; the examples themselves are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.8 documents the arXiv implementation's disabled actions and DeepSeek-R1 configuration. Appendix B newly describes checking search-term provenance during trajectory auditing, without establishing a new sample collection. The code-access link, appendix prompts, model-size information, and token/cost measurements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.2 refines the contribution's positioning from improving evaluation of LLM-generated literature summaries to extending retrieval-based citation recommendation with faithful attribution and valid alternatives. The cited works are retained; the numerous author, year, title, and venue updates are bibliographic changes rather than added literature.

P1.justification: v4 polishes the abstract and introduction, corrects grammar and table references, expands Appendix B, and adds Section 5.8 and acknowledgments. Most paragraphs, section ordering, and appendix organization are retained, so this is a limited editorial revision.

P2.justification: v4 adds the citation-set table and backend table, removes the agreement column from Table 2, and restructures Table 4 for additional domains. The unchanged cost table moves from Table 5 to Table 11. Figure 3 highlights existing actions with a 'NEW' border, Figure 13's caption is corrected, and several displays relocate; the overall visual design remains.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the central comparison through a matched five-run CiteAgent evaluation with uncertainty and corrects the headline gain to approximately 10 percentage points, consistent with Table 2's 45.1% versus 35.4%. Added domain and backend experiments provide useful evidence about generalization and retrieval dependence. These are limited overall gains: the revised Bayesian and agreement values, including construction of Table 5's top-k sets, remain insufficiently explained.
